# Essential Commands and Workshop Keys

## Accessing Images and Image Collections

### Accessing an Image and Viewing Information

``` javascript
// add a single image
var image = ee.Image("image_name");

//this will print information about the image in the console
print(image);
```

### Accessing an Image Collection and Viewing Information

``` javascript
// add an image collection
var image_collection = ee.ImageCollection("image_collection_name");

//this will print information about the first image 
//in the image collection in the console
print(image_collection.first());
```

## Filtering Image Collections

### Filter by a Date Range

``` javascript
// filter by a date
var filtered_collection = image_collection.filterDate('2021-08-01', '2021-08-02');

//filter by a set of dates
var filtered_collection = image_collection.filterDate('2021-08-01', '2022-08-02');

//filter by a year or set of years
var filtered_collection = image_collection.filter(
    ee.Filter.calendarRange(2021, 2023, 'year')
);

//filter by a month
var filtered_collection = image_collection.filter(
    ee.Filter.calendarRange(8, 8, 'month')
);

//filter by day of year
var filtered_collection = image_collection.filter(
    ee.Filter.dayOfYear(150, 200)
);

//filter by day of the month
var filtered_collection = image_collection.filter(
    ee.Filter.calendarRange(1, 15, 'day_of_month')
);
```

### Filter by a Location

Filter an image collection to images that intersect a geometry.

``` javascript
// Filter by a point (coordinates)
var point = ee.Geometry.Point([-122.292, 37.901]);

var filtered_collection = image_collection.filterBounds(point);
```

``` javascript
// Filter by an ee.Geometry, ee.Feature, or ee.FeatureCollection
//in this case roi needs to be an ee.Geometry or ee.FeatureCollection
var filtered_collection = image_collection.filterBounds(roi);
```

### Filter by Metadata Properties

For these, you need to reference the actual metadata to see what the variables are called

``` javascript
//cloud cover less than 10%
var filtered_collection = image_collection.filter(
    ee.Filter.lt('CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE', 10)
);

//cloud cover greater than 10%
var filtered_collection = image_collection.filter(
    ee.Filter.gt('CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE', 10)
);


//cloud cover equal to 10%
var filtered_collection = image_collection.filter(
    ee.Filter.eq('CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE', 10)
);

//cloud cover between 10% and 20%
var filtered_collection = image_collection.filter(
    ee.Filter.and(
        ee.Filter.gte('CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE', 10),
        ee.Filter.lte('CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE', 20)
    )
);
```

## Visualization

### Visualizing a Single-Band

``` javascript

Map.addLayer(
    image, //  image to display
    {
        bands: ['band_name'], //  band to display
        min: min, //  display range  
        max: max
    },
    'Layer Name' //  name to show in Layer Manager
);
```

### Visualizing a Multi-Band

``` javascript

Map.addLayer(
    image, //image to display
    {
        bands: ['SR_B3', 'SR_B2', 'SR_B1'], //bands will automatically fill RGB
        min: min,
        max: max
    },
    'Layer Name' //name to show in Layer Manager
);
```

### Visualizing an Image Collection

The `Map.addLayer` command expects a single image. To visualize an image collection you need to reduce it to a single image. The easiest way to do this is to take the median value for each pixel across the image collection. You can also use `mean()`, `max()`, or `min()` to reduce the image collection.

``` javascript

Map.addLayer(
    image_collection.median(), //takes the median of the image collection
    {
        bands: ['SR_B3', 'SR_B2', 'SR_B1'], //bands will automatically fill RGB
        min: min,
        max: max
    },
    'Layer Name' //name to show in Layer Manager
);
```

### Help Picking Min/Max

An easy way to pick min/max values is to take a sample of the raster and use that to see percentile values

``` javascript

// for an image
var stats = image.select('band')
  .sample({
    region: image.geometry(),
    numPixels: 1000,
    scale: 30
  })
  .reduceColumns({
    reducer: ee.Reducer.percentile([2, 98]),
    selectors: ['band']
  });

print(stats);


// for an image collection
var stats = image_collection.median().select('band')
  .sample({
    region: image_collection.first().geometry(),
    numPixels: 1000,
    scale: 30
  })
  .reduceColumns({
    reducer: ee.Reducer.percentile([2, 98]),
    selectors: ['band']
  });

print(stats);
```

### Using Different Min/Max per band

```javascript
//fill in with bands of interest
var stats = image.select(['B2','B3','B4','B8','B11']).reduceRegion({
    reducer: ee.Reducer.percentile([2, 98]),
    geometry: ch,
    scale: 20,
    maxPixels: 1e9
});

print('2nd and 98th percentile pixel values per band:', stats);

//fill in with bands of interest and values from above
Map.addLayer(
    image, 
    {
        bands: ['B8', 'B4', 'B3'], 
        min: [219, 231, 295],    
        max: [3239, 1630, 1374]  
    }
);


```

### Setting Color Palette for Single-Band Image

Start by adding this [repo](https://code.earthengine.google.com/?accept_repo=users/gena/packages) to your GEE account. You can view all the palette options [here](https://github.com/gee-community/ee-palettes)

``` javascript

var palettes = require('users/gena/packages:palettes');

Map.addLayer(
    image, //  image to display
    {
        bands: ['band_name'], //  band to display
        min: min, //  display range  
        max: max,
        palette: palettes.colorbrewer.RdYlGn[9] //set palette and number of classes
    },
    'Layer Name' //  name to show in Layer Manager
);
```

Or you can manually set palettes:

``` javascript

Map.addLayer(
    image, //  image to display
    {
        bands: ['band_name'], //  band to display
        min: min, //  display range  
        max: max,
        palette: ['blue', 'white', 'green'] //set palette manually
    },
    'Layer Name' //  name to show in Layer Manager
);

```

## Selecting Bands

### Select Bands

``` javascript

// select a single band
var band = image.select('band_name');


// select multiple bands
var bands = image.select(['band_1', 'band_2', 'band_3']);
```

### Rename Bands

``` javascript

// rename a band
var renamed = image.select('old_band_name').rename('new_band_name');
```

## Band Math

Band math allows you to create new raster bands by mathematically combining existing bands. Common operations include addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and normalized differences.

### Basic Mathematical Operations

``` javascript
// select individual bands 

var band_1 = image.select('band_1'); 
var band_2 = image.select('band_2'); 

// add two bands 
var added = band_1.add(band_2); 

// subtract
var subtracted = band_1.subtract(band_2);

// multiply two bands 
var multiplied = band_1.multiply(band_2); 

// divide 
var divided = band_1.divide(band_2);

//built in normalized difference function

var normalized_difference = image.normalizedDifference(['band_1', 'band_2'])
```

### Using Expressions

Expressions can be used for more complicated operations

``` javascript

var calculated_band = image.expression( 
                    '(BAND_1 - BAND_2) / (BAND_1 + BAND_2)', 
                    { BAND_1: image.select('band_1'), 
                    BAND_2: image.select('band_2') });
```

## Thresholds, Reclassifying, and Masking

### Threshold

``` javascript

// greater than a threshold
var thresholded = image.gt(threshold);

// greater than or equal to a threshold
var thresholded = image.gte(threshold);

// less than a threshold
var thresholded = image.lt(threshold);

// less than or equal to a threshold
var thresholded = image.lte(threshold);

// equal to a threshold
var thresholded = image.eq(threshold);
```

### Reclassifying

``` javascript

// create multiple classes
var reclassified = image
    .where(image.lt(threshold_1), value_1)
    .where(
        image.gte(threshold_1)
            .and(image.lt(threshold_2)),
        value_2
    )
    .where(image.gte(threshold_2), value_3);
```

### Masking

``` javascript
// create a mask
var mask = image.gt(threshold);

// apply the mask
var masked_image = image.updateMask(mask);
```

### Cloud Masking

```javascript

//Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 Level 2 
function maskLandsatClouds(image) {
  // Select the QA band that stores per-pixel quality flags
  var qa = image.select('QA_PIXEL');
  // Bit 1 = dilated cloud, 2 = cirrus, 3 = cloud, 4 = cloud shadow
  var badBits = (1 << 1) | (1 << 2) | (1 << 3) | (1 << 4);
  // A pixel is clear if NONE of those bits are turned on
  var clear = qa.bitwiseAnd(badBits).eq(0);
  // Keep the clear pixels, drop everything else
  return image.updateMask(clear);
}

// Sentinel-2 SR Harmonized, masked with Cloud Score+
function maskS2clouds(image) {
  // Look up this image's matching Cloud Score+ image by its ID
  var csPlus = ee.ImageCollection('GOOGLE/CLOUD_SCORE_PLUS/V1/S2_HARMONIZED');
  var match = csPlus.filter(
    ee.Filter.eq('system:index', image.get('system:index'))).first();
  // Scores run 0 (occluded) to 1 (clear)
  var score = ee.Image(match).select('cs_cdf');
  // A pixel is clear if its score is at or above the threshold
  var clear = score.gte(0.60);
  // Keep the clear pixels, drop everything else
  return image.updateMask(clear);
}


```

### Clipping Images

```javascript

var clipped = image.clip(roi);
```

## Image Composites

```javascript
// median composite
var composite = image_collection.median();

// mean composite
var composite = image_collection.mean();

// minimum value composite
var composite = image_collection.min();

// maximum value composite
var composite = image_collection.max();

// sum composite
var composite = image_collection.sum();
```

## Mapping Functions Over Image Collections

### Defining a Function
``` javascript
var function_name = function(image){

    //perform operations here

    return image;

};
```

### Map a Function

```javascript
var processed_collection =
    image_collection.map(function_name);

```

### Reduce Image by Region

```javascript

var projection = image.projection();

var output = image.reduceRegions({
    collection: feature_collection,
    reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(),
    scale: projection.nominalScale(),
    crs: projection
});

```

## Workshop 2 Answer Key
```javascript

//GEOG 567 Workshop #2 Answer Key
//Vegetation health in the southern San Joaquin Valley, 2019 vs 2022


//define study area
var studyarea = ee.Geometry.Polygon(
        [[-120.19993930468863, 36.826631173862694],
          [-120.19993930468863, 35.37984489565024],
          [-118.91453891406363, 35.37984489565024],
          [-118.91453891406363, 36.826631173862694]]);

Map.centerObject(studyarea, 8);


//define cloud mask function for sentinel-2
function maskS2clouds(image) {
  // Look up this image's matching Cloud Score+ image by its ID
  var csPlus = ee.ImageCollection('GOOGLE/CLOUD_SCORE_PLUS/V1/S2_HARMONIZED');
  var match = csPlus.filter(
    ee.Filter.eq('system:index', image.get('system:index'))).first();
  // Scores run 0 (occluded) to 1 (clear)
  var score = ee.Image(match).select('cs_cdf');
  // A pixel is clear if its score is at or above the threshold
  var clear = score.gte(0.60);
  // Keep the clear pixels, drop everything else
  return image.updateMask(clear);
}


//I chose the median because it takes the middle value at each pixel, so any
//clouds or shadows that the mask missed (which are unusually bright or dark)
//will not pull the composite the way they would with the mean. Max would
//favor leftover clouds and min would favor shadows.

//filter data, apply cloud mask, take median, clip, scale
var pre = ee.ImageCollection("COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED")
                            .filterBounds(studyarea)
                            .filterDate('2019-07-01', '2019-09-01')
                            .map(maskS2clouds)
                            .median()
                            .clip(studyarea)
                            .divide(10000);

Map.addLayer(pre, {bands: ['B4', 'B3', 'B2'], min: 0, max: 0.3}, '2019 true color');


//filter data, apply cloud mask, take median, clip, scale
var post = ee.ImageCollection("COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED")
                            .filterBounds(studyarea)
                            .filterDate('2022-07-01', '2022-09-01')
                            .map(maskS2clouds)
                            .median()
                            .clip(studyarea)
                            .divide(10000);

Map.addLayer(post, {bands: ['B4', 'B3', 'B2'], min: 0, max: 0.3}, '2022 true color');


//WRITE A FUNCTION TO CALCULATE EVI (this creates an image with ONLY EVI)

var calcEVI = function(image){
    var evi = image.expression(
        '2.5 * ((NIR - RED) / (NIR + 6 * RED - 7.5 * BLUE + 1))',
        {
            NIR: image.select('B8'),
            RED: image.select('B4'),
            BLUE: image.select('B2')
        }
    ).rename('EVI');
    return evi;
};

//pre and post are single images (the median turned each collection into
//one image), so we call the function directly on them
var evi_pre = calcEVI(pre);
var evi_post = calcEVI(post);



//IF YOU WANTED TO WRITE A FUNCTION TO ADD EVI AS A BAND

var addEVI = function(image){
    var evi = image.expression(
        '2.5 * ((NIR - RED) / (NIR + 6 * RED - 7.5 * BLUE + 1))',
        {
            NIR: image.select('B8'),
            RED: image.select('B4'),
            BLUE: image.select('B2')
        }
    ).rename('EVI');
    return image.addBands(evi);
};

//call the function directly, then select the EVI band

//     {
//         NIR: pre.select('B8'),
//         RED: pre.select('B4'),
//         BLUE: pre.select('B2')
//     }
// ).rename('EVI');

//     {
//         NIR: post.select('B8'),
//         RED: post.select('B4'),
//         BLUE: post.select('B2')
//     }
// ).rename('EVI');



//visualize EVI for each year
Map.addLayer(evi_pre, {min: 0, max: 0.8, palette: ['white', 'green']}, 'EVI 2019');
Map.addLayer(evi_post, {min: 0, max: 0.8, palette: ['white', 'green']}, 'EVI 2022');


//calculate the change in EVI (2022 minus 2019)
//negative values mean EVI went down during the drought
var evi_change = evi_post.subtract(evi_pre);

Map.addLayer(evi_change, {min: -0.5, max: 0.5, palette: ['red', 'white', 'green']}, 'EVI change');


//binary classification: 1 where EVI decreased by more than 0.10, 0 everywhere else
var evi_decline = evi_change.lt(-0.10);

Map.addLayer(evi_decline, {min: 0, max: 1, palette: ['white', 'red']}, 'EVI decline > 0.10');


//SUMMARY
//The largest EVI declines are on the west side of the study area (western
//Fresno and Kings counties and northwestern Kern County, around Huron,
//Kettleman City, and Lost Hills) and in the old Tulare Lake bed. The declines
//show up as whole, sharp-edged rectangular fields, and many fields that were
//green in 2019 look like bare soil in the 2022 true color composite. The east
//side of the valley and the orchard areas change much less, and the cities
//(Fresno, Visalia, Bakersfield) show little change.
//
//This pattern most likely represents fallowing. West side growers depend
//heavily on surface water deliveries, and when allocations were cut in 2022,
//many fields were left unplanted. The field-by-field shape of the change shows that this is a land management
//decision, not gradual drought stress on the vegetation, which would look
//more spread out.
```
